Regression probe (temporary edit to budget-pause.test.ts W15B-14, then restored): the review-only session's events are [..., task.started(reviewOnly), critic.review_started, critic.review, critic.verdict, docs.status_written, critic.session_review_metrics, critic.session_review, session.ended]. The last task.started/task.finished before session.ended is the review-only task.started. See the blocking item.

blocking.issue: W15B-14's review-only line is a task.started event that never gets a task.finished. Four readers treat 'last task.started' as the task in flight, so after the critic's verdict the session page, the project header and the chat context keep saying the reviewed task is running until the session ends (design §5 rule 4, true now). This is a regression in neighbouring behaviour: at the base nothing claimed a task in flight there.
blocking.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1584 (emit task.started {specialist:'critic', reviewOnly:true}); readers: packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1610-1621 (liveSessionView currentTask), packages/runtime/src/daemon/project-status.ts:515-524 (workingOn), packages/runtime/src/conversation/project-facts.ts:189-201 (chat '# Working now'), apps/ui/src/lib/session-steps.ts:37-49 (currentFromLog, the session page's Current task card and the drawer's steps)
blocking.evidence: runner.ts:1844 emits task.finished only `if (!result.reviewOnly)`, and docs/maintainers/runtime.md:2877-2880 says the review-only pass has 'no task.finished' and 'Its only start is a task.started'. A temporary probe in budget-pause.test.ts 'W15B-14: the waiting review's session ...' printed the second session's events: [..., 'task.started(reviewOnly)', 'critic.review_started', 'critic.review', 'critic.verdict', 'docs.status_written', 'critic.session_review_metrics', 'critic.session_review', 'session.ended']. The last task.started/finished before session.ended is {type:'task.started', payload:{title:'Index page', specialist:'critic', reviewOnly:true}}. So after the verdict, while the status doc is written and the session review (a critic model call, seconds to a minute with the real model) runs: GET /sessions/:id returns currentTask 'Index page' (critic), the session page shows Current task '"Index page" · critic' next to 'Stop now' ('Stops the current task at once'), the project header says 'Alice is working on "Index page"', and the chat context says 'A session on X is running: "Index page" (the critic)'. By then the task is done (accepted) or its card is already in the Inbox. At the base the review-only pass emitted no task.started, so these readers said 'Choosing the next task…' / between tasks.
blocking.expected: The review-only line must not leave a task 'in flight' after its verdict. Either end it (for example a closing event the four readers treat as an end, or end at critic.verdict when the start was reviewOnly), or write the line as an event those readers do not count as a start. Add a test at the boundary the person reads: GET /sessions/:id currentTask and project workingOn are null after the verdict while the session still runs (e.g. hold the session review), plus currentFromLog over the same event sequence.

non_blocking: packages/runtime/test/writing-rules.test.ts:718 dropped the assertion that the plan card's runs-on line is at most 100 characters (design §5 rule 1). Naming up to three titles cut at 40 characters can make the line about 190 characters, and the test now has no bound at all. A wider bound would keep the protection, for example ≤ 100 plus the three quoted titles.

Sibling of W15B-14, neither fixed nor logged: the session result (summary and chip) still says '"X" ... need your decision (Inbox).' for a task whose card is a specialist's questions card. Bench walk 4: '"Choose the `colours` for the **club** in colours.md" and "Draft the poster text in poster.md" need your decision (Inbox).', while the card says ': the specialist asks you'.

W15B-79's new fallback applies to a person task that reaches a session. executor.ts:854's summary now gives the log line '"Confirm the colours with the human" could not run: Waiting for your answers in the Inbox (2 questions); no specialist ran (Inbox).': a capital mid-sentence, and 'could not run' for a question task.
